mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (below 0.1%) signals accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the market prices in continued liquidity support.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1% (as measured at decision time).

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate exceeding 6.5% indicates deteriorating labor market conditions that trigger recession fears, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors reduce equity exposure.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods following UNRATE readings above 6.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) signals robust consumer and business activity, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days through improved corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and INDPRO increase by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: Strong retail sales growth (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% month-over-month indicates sustained consumer spending momentum, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days as the market anticipates elevated corporate revenues in late-cycle expansion.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS growth exceeds 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 100,000 jobs signals strengthening labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods following PAYEMS increases of at least 100,000 jobs.

mechanism_narrative: Accelerating inflation (CPIAUCSL annualized > 2.0%) triggers expectations of monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days as investors price in higher discount rates and reduced corporate margins.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods following CPIAUCSL readings above 2.0% annualized.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) and high unemployment (UNRATE > 6.5%) signals aggressive monetary stimulus in response to labor market weakness, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days as the market anticipates economic support.
regime_hint: monetary stimulus in weak labor market
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% and UNRATE is above 6.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A recovery in industrial production (INDPRO growth > 0.3% month-over-month) following a prior decline signals improving manufacturing activity, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days through elevated capital expenditure expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO growth exceeds 0.3% month-over-month.
